article_text:
He may not be a household name when it comes to the world of jazz, but the influence of Marcus Belgrave is felt far and wide, playing with Ray Charles, Charles Mingus, the Funk Brothers, and more. His life story now gets the documentary treatment with …And Damn He Could Play: The Marcus Belgrave Story , directed by Timashion Jones and featuring narration from Wendell Pierce. Ahead of its DOC NYC world premiere on November 13, we’re pleased to exclusively debut the first trailer and poster.

The documentary features quite the lineup of appearances, including Wynton Marsalis, Don Was, Terence Blanchard, Bert Daring, Bill Meyer, Carl Craig, Charlie Gabriel, Chris Collins, Christopher Smith, Daphne Nitiri, David Ritz, Duke Fakir, Dwight Adams, Endea Owens, Eudora Muhammad, Gayelynn McKinney, Herb Boyd, James Carter, Joan Belgrave, Kasan Belgrave, Karriem Riggins, Mable John, Marion Hayden, Nicholas Peyton, Paul Riser, Ray Parker Jr., Regina Carter, Robert Hurst, Sheila Jordan, Theo Croker, Tonya Hood, and Wendell Harrison.

Here’s the synopsis: “A jazz legend you likely haven’t heard of, trumpet player Marcus Belgrave’s influence has reverberated far beyond the spotlight. Making his professional debut at the age of 12, Belgrave went on to perform and record with the likes of Ray Charles, Charles Mingus, and Motown’s legendary Funk Brothers. Mentored by trumpet icon Clifford Brown, Belgrave in turn became a guiding force for generations of musicians through his work as an educator and mentor, championing Detroit’s artistic soul, and involvement in the groundbreaking arts collective Tribe. His reach can be heard in the artistry of jazz luminaries including Geri Allen, Kenny Garrett, James Carter, Regina Carter, Theo Croker, and Endea Owens, among many others. Though too often overlooked in the broader story of jazz, Belgrave’s legacy lives on in the musicians he inspired, the Detroit scene he helped cultivate, and the music that continues to swing, soar, and speak through generations.”

“As a filmmaker from Detroit, I have always been drawn to stories that show the power of reaching and teaching the next generation. The children are our future, and it is only right that we pour into them and pass the baton so they can run and lead us forward. That is exactly what Marcus did through his music and mentorship,” said director Timashion Jones. “This documentary is my way of honoring that spirit and showing the world how one man could be a shattered diamond who shared his light and love for music with people all across the world. His story reminds us that when you invest in others, your legacy continues to play long after your final note.”

See the exclusive trailer and poster premiere below.

article_text:
濱田祐史が渋谷 MINAで始まるMINA WORLD COLLEGEにて、全10回のラーニングプログラム「見ることのプラクティス／Practices of Seeing」を開催する。申込締め切りは9月13日まで。

本ワークショップでは濱田祐史と約1年をかけて、「見る」という行為によって、どのように世界を認識しているのかを学び、考察する。写真の歴史を学び、身の周りのものからピンホールカメラを制作し、写真を自ら編集し、太陽光で像を定着させるサイアノタイプを体験する。それらの実践を振り返りながら、最終的には空間展示という形で成果発表を行うという。またゲストには山西もも、若山満大（東京ステーションギャラリー学芸員）、鈴木理策、小林孝行（flotsambooks）、伊藤貴弘（東京都写真美術館学芸員）などが登場する。ラーニングプログラムの記録集をグラフィックデザイナーの星加陸が手掛けるなど、様々なゲストで彩られワークショップは進行していく予定だ。

「Practice of Seeing｜見ることのプラクティス」は、「見ること」を起点に、「まだ見えていないもの」に気づき、世界を楽しむ選択肢を広げていくための実践講座。ぜひ体験してみたい。

タイトル

濱田祐史「見ることのプラクティス／Practices of Seeing」

MINA（150-0002 東京都渋谷区渋谷3-7-1）

月1回開催の写真コース 19:00〜21:30

9月13日〆切

"在以芝加哥为背景的《理发店》中，她强调要反映当时的社区风貌与时尚。罗杰斯补充道：“一位教授曾告诫我，现代服装设计将是我做过最难的事情。演员们会带着一个想法——或者毫无想法——走进剧组，然后，在围读剧本之后，一切都会改变。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "菲利普斯的作品包括《夜行动物》、《The Invite》和《我想要你的爱》，她指出人们对现代服装设计常常存在误解。“我曾和制片厂高管共处一室。导演、编剧、制片人和制片厂高管——他们很有钱。他们赚很多钱。他们和购物、或是有人帮他们购物有着密切的联系。他们买得起自己想要的东西，而且他们自己就是专家。这种情况在演员身上经常发生，他们会说，‘哦，我知道我的角色穿过那些普拉达靴子。’正如玛丽所说，你必须成为你角色的推销员。服装设计很容易被那些坐在办公桌后面摆弄数字、却不给你提供所需支持的人所不尊重。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "菲利普斯还探讨了随着奢侈品牌进入融资领域，产品植入在服装设计中日益增长的影响力。“制片人会告诉我们，‘你必须使用那个产品。’你必须选择那些支持忠于故事本身的导演，因为随着电影融资方式的变化，这只会变得越来越复杂。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "设计师们还分享了对他们最新作品的见解。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "埃伦·米罗尼克为克里斯托弗·诺兰打造了5300多套戏服，其中重点聚焦于安妮·海瑟薇饰演的佩涅洛佩王后。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "伊萨卡王宫的色彩主题是焦红色，这在整部电影佩涅洛佩的戏服中得到了体现。米罗尼克解释道：“让她保持这些色调非常重要，这样才不会破坏故事。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在奥德修斯归来的高潮时刻，佩涅洛佩穿着一件蓝色的礼服，这件礼服成为了她的铠甲。“我们用细密的褶皱制作了一种垂坠感，非常紧身且契合她的身体轮廓。它一直延伸到她的脖颈，配上一条金项链——这是她佩戴的仅有的几件装饰品之一。这让人感觉她已经准备好战斗，并且要独当一面。她要迎接一项挑战，而她的礼服则强化了她的力量。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾与罗伯特·埃格斯合作过《北方人》和《Werwulf》的穆尔谈到了她对羊毛的细致研究，在维京时代，羊毛是一种代表财富的商品。穆尔解释道：“不列颠群岛上没有狼，因为国王下令将它们全部消灭，以免它们吃掉绵羊。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "富人们购买那些羊毛，因此任何拥有大量羊毛服装的人都属于上流社会。穆尔力求真实，但她表示：“这些电影的挑战在于寻找能够制作羊毛织物、帽子、珠宝、纽扣、皮带的人——当可供使用的风格和元素如此之少时，所有这些细节共同构成了完整的画面。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "菲利普斯谈到了她在《The Invite》中与奥利维娅·王尔德的合作。“这是我第三次与奥利维娅合作，因此彼此之间有很高的信任度。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "菲利普斯仅通过一次换装来定下基调。克鲁斯的戏服经过了精心分层，随着故事的发展展现出关于她的更多细节。王尔德饰演的安吉拉是一位失去了创造力的全职艺术家。菲利普斯说：“我与制作设计师杰德·希利（Jade Healy）合作，确保她能融入背景墙中。”她接着说：“我想让赛思的色调与之相似，而蓝色真的让我很困扰，因为它们不够和谐。后来我意识到这其实非常完美，因为这种关系本身就是不同步的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗杰斯谈到了参与《穿普拉达的女王2》所面临的挑战。“第一部电影太受喜爱了，我为此琢磨了很久。那是一个完美的组合——剧本、演员、服装。我想：‘好吧，这就是续集的魔咒。’\"", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但她成功做到了。她甚至把那件标志性的天蓝色毛衣带了回来，因为安迪（安妮·海瑟薇）在历经这么多年后依然会留着它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗杰斯透露：“安妮手里拿着剪刀。我原本想把它弄得更自然破旧一点，就像那种你留着不舍得扔、手肘处有洞的毛衣。但她把袖子剪掉了，我意识到它现在变成了一件背心。我当时想在她身上稍微融入一点男装风格，所以它呈现出那种感觉——这是一件背心。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艾米·罗斯（Amy Roth）回顾了《我演洛奇》（I Play Rocky）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她透露，原版《洛奇》电影并没有服装设计师，因此没有参考资料可供借鉴。她说：“重现这个标志性的造型——不仅是电影里的，还有我记忆中以及每个人对洛奇的集体记忆——帽子、皮夹克、手套、弹力球，这些都至关重要。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗斯解释说，这件皮夹克极其重要。“我们不得不把它制作出来并做旧。我在eBay上找到了原版夹克，正好是我饰演该角色的演员的尺码，当时松了一口气。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她将这项工作以及自己成果的提升归功于演员安东尼·伊波利托（Anthony Ippolito）。“他希望自己的身材看起来和史泰龙一模一样。他摆出史泰龙的姿势。他完全融入了那个体形。他真的很想配合我们的工作。他会带来自己穿过的一些东西的照片，然后我们为他进行复刻。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗杰斯还谈到了她对《迈克尔》（Michael）一书的工作以及对《颤栗》（Thriller）MV的重现。她说：“这是我们拍摄的最后几场戏之一。我有一本800页的研究手册，黛博拉·兰迪斯（Deborah Landis）跟我说过一件很有趣的事。我们都知道那件皮夹克是标志性的，但她透露迈克尔的Levi's牛仔裤原本是白色的，她不得不把它们染成红色。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Levi's与电影制作人进行了合作，寄来了几条裤子来重现这个造型。“我有一本潘通色卡，并复刻了那件镶珠夹克，我意识到其中有两种不同的红色色调——色彩饱和度太重要了，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一切都在于捕捉每一个细节，而僵尸舞者也同样重要。“我想：‘那是穿粉红色裙子的女人。我必须把珍珠放在这个位置。’\"", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "请在下方观看完整对话。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Contrary to popular belief, contemporary design in film is not just about shopping; it involves deep storytelling and thought behind how characters are dressed.

Molly Rogers, who worked on “The Devil Wears Prada” as an assistant costume designer and was the sequel’s costume designer, said, “When someone comes up to me and says, ‘I really want to learn and work with you. I love to shop.’ That’s an automatic exit.”

Related Stories

Why Did Netflix Boot Bela Bajaria?

Netflix’s 'Haunted Hotel' Renewed for Season 3

Rogers spoke at the Costume Design Roundtable at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival , moderated by Variety’s Senior Artisans Editor Jazz Tangcay. Joining her were Ellen Mirojnick (“The Odyssey”), Arianne Phillips (“The Invite”), Linda Muir (“Werwulf”), Amy Roth (“I Play Rocky”) and Marci Rodgers (“Michael”).

Mirojnick, known for her work on “Wall Street,” “Basic Instinct” and “Fatal Attraction,” discussed the challenges of contemporary costume design. “In the beginning of my career, I did a lot of contemporary costume, and I loved it. I loved being able to document what New York was like at that period, because yes, it was for film, but it also documented the history of what we were like, even if it was an elevated contemporary character.” She added, “Contemporary design is very difficult and very beautiful at the same time to create.”

Rodgers recalled her first job on Spike Lee’s “She’s Gotta Have It.” Coming from Chicago, she knew New York’s style was different, so she asked Lee to sit with her during background casting. “So I could see how people are coming in here dressed.” When developing Nola Darling’s wardrobe, she learned the character’s favorite artist was Prince. “Purple is clearly going to be a thing. But it would be tidbits of purple. She wouldn’t shop at Saks.” Rodgers focused on thrift stores for Nola’s look.

On “Barbershop,” set in Chicago, she emphasized reflecting the community and fashion of the moment. Rodgers added, “A professor cautioned me that contemporary design would be the hardest thing I’d ever do. Actors will come in with an idea — or no idea — and then, after the table read, everything changes.”

Phillips, whose credits include “Nocturnal Animals,” “The Invite” and “I Want Your Sex,” noted that contemporary design is often misunderstood. “I’ve been in rooms with studio executives. Directors, writers, producers and studio executives — they’re rich. They make a lot of money. They have a relationship to shopping, someone shopping for them. They can afford what they want, and they’re experts. This happens with actors a lot, where they’ll say, ‘Oh, I know my character wore those Prada boots.’ You have to be, as Marci said, a salesperson for your character. Costume design can be disrespected so easily by people sitting behind desks moving numbers around and not giving you the support you need.”

Phillips also discussed the increasing influence of product placement in costume design as luxury brands enter the financing space. “We’re told by producers, ‘You have to use that product.’ You have to choose directors who support staying true to the story, as this is only going to get more complicated with how films are financed.”

The designers also shared insights into their latest projects.

Ellen Mirojnick crafted over 5,300 costumes for Christopher Nolan, focusing on Anne Hathaway’s Queen Penelope.

The House of Ithaca’s color theme was burned red, which was reflected in Penelope’s costumes throughout the film. Mirojnick explained, “It was very important to keep her in those tones, not to disrupt the story.”

At the climactic moment when Odysseus returns, Penelope wears a blue dress that serves as her armor. “We created a drape with fine pleats, very tight and specific to the shape of her body. It went up through her neck, paired with a golden necklace — one of the only decorative pieces she wears. It felt as if she was ready for battle, and she was going to hold her own. She had a challenge to put forth, and her gown reinforced her strength.”

Muir, who worked with Robert Eggers on “The Northman” and “Werwulf,” spoke about her meticulous research on wool, a commodity in Viking times that denoted wealth. Muir explained, “There are no wolves in the British Isles because the king ordered all of them eradicated so they wouldn’t eat the sheep.”

The wealthy bought that wool, so anyone with a lot of wool clothing was upper class. Muir strove for authenticity but said, “The challenge with these films is finding people who can create wool fabrics, hats, jewelry, buttons, belts — all the things that make the whole picture when you have so few styles and elements to work with.”

Phillips discussed her work with Olivia Wilde on “The Invite.” “It was my third time working with Olivia, so there’s a lot of trust there.”

Phillips used only one costume change to set the tone. Cruz’s costume was layered intentionally to reveal more about her as the story progressed. Wilde’s Angela is a stay-at-home artist who had lost her creativity. Phillips said, “I worked with production designer Jade Healy to make sure she blended into the walls.” She continued, “I wanted Seth’s palette to be similar, and the blues were really bothering me because they weren’t in harmony. Then I realized that was perfect because the relationship is out of sync..”

Rogers discussed the challenges of working on “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” “The first movie is so beloved, and I meditated on that for a while. It was a perfect storm — the script, the cast, the clothing. I thought, ‘OK, the curse of the sequel.’”

But she pulled it off. She even brought back the iconic cerulean sweater because Andy (Anne Hathaway) would still have it after all these years.

Rogers revealed, “Annie had scissors in her hands. I had wanted to shred it more naturally, like the sweater with holes in the elbows that you hang on to. But she chopped the sleeves off, and I realized it’s now a vest. I was trying to do menswear a little with her, so it read that way — it’s a vest.”

Amy Roth reflected on “I Play Rocky.”

She revealed the original “Rocky” film didn’t have a costume designer, so there were no references to pull from. She said, “Recreating this iconic look — not just from the film, but from my memory and everybody’s collective memory of Rocky — the hat, the leather jacket, the gloves, the bouncing ball, they were all crucial.”

Roth explained that the leather jacket was so important. “We had to make it and age it. I found the original jacket on eBay, in my actor’s size and felt relief.”

She credits actor Anthony Ippolito for elevating the work and her work. “He wanted his body to look exactly like Stallone’s. He posed like Stallone. He just embodied his body. He really wanted to do what we were doing. He would bring pictures of things he wore, and we’d recreate them for him.”

Rogers also touched upon her work on “Michael” and recreating the “Thriller” video. She said, “It was one of the last things we shot. I had a research book of 800 pages, and Deborah Landis told me something interesting. We all know the leather jacket is iconic, but she revealed that Michael’s Levi jeans were originally white and she had to dye them red.”

Levi’s collaborated with the filmmakers, sending a few pairs to recreate the look. “I had a Pantone book and recreated the beaded jacket, realizing there were two different shades of red — color value is so important,” she said.

It was all about capturing every detail, and the zombie dancers mattered just as much. “I thought, ‘That’s the woman in the pink dress. I’ve got to put the pearls right here.”

article_text:
The wait is over, Portrait of Britain Vol. 9 is now open for entries!

Real people. Real lives. Real faces. Since 2016, this award has asked photographers to share the stories of the people they meet every day: family members, local legends, and famous faces alike.

For volume 8, Alex Elton-Wall photographed 170 of his Lydbrook neighbours on a fly-tipped sofa that became a village-wide art installation whilst Jaiyana Chelikha photographed Jounaid, born and raised in the UK, on Dartmoor in a gandoura, a traditional North African robe, worn over streetwear.

From the entries, 200 portraits will be shortlisted and 100 will be named winners. Those 100 will be shown on JCDecaux UK digital screens across the country for a month from early January 2027, turning the British high street into a nationwide gallery.

BJP Members can enter up to 10 images for free, plus get digital access to the latest issue POLITICS on their Online Library.

article_text:
目頭を押さえつつ熱い拍手と歓声の観客

新国立劇場バレエ団の2026／2027シーズンの幕開けを飾る新制作「街の灯」。新国立劇場（東京）で行われた10月23日の世界初演は、期待に違わぬ高い完成度で、終演後は目頭を押さえつつ、スタンディングオベーションで熱い拍手と歓声を贈る観客の姿が目立ち、カーテンコールがなかなか終わりませんでした。大成功の初日といってよいでしょう。カンパニーの総合力の高さを示しました。

振付、舞台、音楽の充実

チャップリンの不朽の名作「街の灯」（1931年）を世界で初めてバレエ化した本プロダクション。幼少期からこの映画に親しんでいたというアラスター・マリオットさんの振付は、チャップリンに対する深いリスペクトを示すように、映画の展開をほぼ踏襲して進み、細かいエピソードまで忠実に再現しているのには驚かされました。映画のシークエンスを尊重しているため、全幕のバレエ作品としても場面転換がかなり多いのですが、舞台機構と美術と照明、そして音楽を巧みにつかってテンポよく切り替え、温まった舞台と客席を終幕まで繋ぎました。ディック・バードさん（美術・衣裳）、エレン・ルーゲさん（照明）らスタッフの確かな力量でしょう。

チャップリン自作の音楽をオーケストレーションし、指揮も務めたティモシー・ブロックさんはさすがチャップリン研究の専門家だけあって、自ら制作した複雑なスコアをしっかり整理してピットをまとめていました。変拍子が多く、テンポも情緒も頻繁に変化する難曲に食らいついた東京フィルハーモニー交響楽団も大健闘。カーテンコールで大きな拍手をもらっていました。

コール・ド・バレエ、やはり新国の華

ダンサー陣は見事のひとことです。まず挙げたいのは新国バレエ団が誇るコール・ド・バレエのますますの充実ぶりです。冒頭、街ゆく市民たちの活気あふれる姿を迫力のアップテンポの群舞で生き生きと表現。一気に劇場を「街の灯」の世界に引き込みました。その後もナイトクラブやラストの場面など、芝居のギアが変わる勘所で群舞が大きな役割を果たし、鮮やかでした。

奥村さん、米沢さん、スクリーンから抜け出したよう

主役の奥村康祐さん（リトル・トランプ）、米沢唯さん（盲目の花売り娘）は映画のスクリーンからそのまま飛び出してきたようでした。

リトル・トランプはほとんど出ずっぱりのタフな役柄で、有名なボクシングや警官からの逃走劇など激しい場面も多く、最終盤に最大の見せ場のパ・ド・ドゥが待っているという難役。奥村さんはチャップリンが乗り移ったかのように大いに笑わせ、涙を誘い、見事でした。娘への真摯な愛と貧困ゆえの哀しみ、微妙な心理の綾が客席に伝わってきました。

花売り娘について「かわいそうな人でない」と語っていた米沢さんは、そのとおり主体的に力強く生きる女性を説得力を持って演じ切りました。「目が見えない」キャラクターの繊細な表現で登場の場面から観客の視線をくぎ付けに。そして境遇の変化。終幕の姿はやはり涙なしには見られないものでした。

キャストもスキなし

中盤のスペクタクルな見せ場で主役となった「ムービースター」の福岡雄大さん、木村優里さんは役柄どおりのスターの貫禄とテクニックでした。けれんみたっぷりに舞台を盛り上げました。

ドラマのカギを握る宇賀大将さん（執事）、直塚美穂さん（メイド）が実力者ならではの芸達者ぶりで目が覚めるよう。いつもどおり切れ味鋭い演技を見せた直塚さんは特に拍手をたくさんもらっていました。大富豪（中家正博さん）も笑いをしっかりとっていました。

「貧困」「格差」を考える舞台

原作の映画で「貧困」や「格差」が大きなテーマのひとつであることは改めて言うまでもないのですが、舞台作品として生身の人間が目の前でキャラクターに命を吹き込むと、その重みが一層、見る側に迫ってきます。

この厳しい時代にリブートされるに相応しい「街の灯」。国内外のバレエファンはもちろん、演劇ファンや映画ファンにもぜひ見てほしい歴史的なプロダクションになりました。11月1日まで９公演、可能であればぜひ劇場に足を運んで、体感してほしい舞台です。（「美術展ナビ」編集長 岡部匡志）

◇喜劇王チャップリンの名作『街の灯』 新国立劇場バレエ団が世界初のバレエ化！ 10月23日開幕

◇新国立劇場バレエ団「街の灯」で公開リハーサル 奥村康祐さん、米沢唯さんが出会いの場面など披露 心情を細やかに写す圧巻の演技 世界初演に高まる期待

◇新国立劇場バレエ団 プリンシパルの柴山紗帆さんに聞く 「経験を積み、演技の引き出しが増えた」 新制作「街の灯」は「コメディ要素豊富で、かつ深い感動のある作品に」

◇新国立劇場バレエ団「街の灯」で主役に抜擢の石山蓮さん 「キャスティングを知り、食事がのどを通らず」「心の温まる世界観が表現される『街の灯』」「バレエへの向き合い方を変えてくれた監督のひとこと」

editorial_excerpt_zh: 在北京艺术家施国威于深圳全新开幕的 Fotografiska 影像艺术中心举办的个展“Festa”中，他那些经过手工上色的摄影作品揭示了欢庆边缘的不安与忧郁。陈静茹（Michele Chan）

"对面的墙上悬挂着一幅大尺幅的画作《鼓》（2026），这是他将于今年 10 月在深圳 Fotografiska 首次亮相的一系列全新创作之一。在一处平淡无奇的地板上，错落着一组红色的庆典鼓，画面上方依稀可见一根同样平淡无奇的柱子的基座。拍摄视角微微向下倾斜，透出一种偶然感，但事实并非如此——这些乐器零落散乱，带有一种令人不安的、近乎有知觉般的张力。", "translated": true}, "“它们或许在不久前刚刚被敲响，”施国威说，“随后便被抛在一旁，人们则转去投入别的狂欢。”施国威的创作方法始于黑白照片，他用水性颜料以严苛而细致的笔触在其上反复罩染，以此追求他所谓的“真实的幻觉”。手工着色是一项严谨且早已大面积过时的技术，它早于彩色摄影的诞生。施国威曾在清华大学美术学院和德国多特蒙德应用技术大学接受摄影训练，他复兴并重新调配了这种古老的方法——不是为了逼真，而是为了用一种特定的情感强度，即他所称的“触觉真实”，来置换被记录的事实。在这里，污渍斑斑的地板凹槽泛着被灼烧般的红陶色。鼓身上的贴金因生锈而黯淡，暗红漆面因岁月的磨损与污渍而斑驳。然而，它们的鼓面却依然呈现出一种突兀的、格格不入的雪白色，其上方隐约可见“百年行”字样。", "“有一段时间，我发现自己被节日吸引，”施国威告诉我，“但不是因为它们的盛大场面。吸引我的是我在节日期间或节日过后所感受到的一种特质。”他近期的创作标志着一种转变：在耗费十年时间描绘草木、山石与植物之后，他将目光转向了人类狂欢的残余物——它的溢出、它的沉淀、它的余温。在远离人群的孤立时刻，或者在嘉年华场地的空旷角落里，施国威捕捉到了一种类似于忧郁却又更为奇异的东西——更为微妙，却又某种程度上更为锐利。在《鼓》中，这种情绪在这些经过使用而褪色、却因此更显力量的酒红色鼓筒中渗透得最为强烈。这种色调与旁边悬挂的一幅小得多的方形习作遥相呼应：那是一幅岩石质感的特写，也是施国威目前——至少暂时——最为人熟知的题材。石头同样泛着鲜活的朱红色，其大理石般的纹理如生肉中的肌理般起伏流转。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "节日通过回归来划分时间。每一次重现都呼唤着欢庆，却也衡量着期间流逝的一切——进步与永恒的幻觉被无形的缺席与失落的账目所消解。一年、一个纪念日、又一场灯光下的聚会——施国威便栖身于这些聚会的阴影之中。“人们把节日理解为充满快乐与希望的集体时刻，”他说，“但我感兴趣的是个人的体验。私人情感可能会与喧嚣和骚动大相径庭。我想探问快乐究竟是什么。”", "translated": true}, "多年来，施国威一直忠于一套取自自然世界的母题词汇，这些母题大多是在独自的山间漫步中累积起来的。我翻阅着一本早期作品的目录：以极其细腻的笔触勾勒出的郁郁葱葱的灌木丛、险峻崎岖的峭壁立面、在饱和粉彩色调中生机勃勃且略带辛辣的多肉植物。它们表面的静止掩盖了其创作所特有的时间性。一张照片将一次相遇压缩为瞬间；施国威则逆转了这个过程，将那个孤立的瞬间重新植入体感时间的蜿蜒流变之中。在几个月的时间里，他通过色彩和反复的落笔，不断重新审视单一的曝光。这种持续的回归带有某种近乎惩罚的意味，但同时也伴随着一种享受：一种重新观看、重新感受的责任。这个过程等同于一场回顾性的相遇，它在色彩上将图像从快门的掌控中解放出来；色彩不再只是信息，而是变成了定性的、活生生的持续时间。在一个以即时编辑和滤镜为组织逻辑的影像文化中，施国威提出了一个近乎愚拙的主张：“有些事情需要时间。”", "当我继续翻阅这本专集时，一种本能的退缩驱使我翻过了一页；回过神来，我又翻了回去。画面看似是一处无害的路边丛林特写；前景中夹竹桃丛的后方，燃烧着一道猩红的地平线——沉闷却又带着狂热，几乎透着恶意。短暂的沉默过后，艺术家开口了。“几年前，有一只小狗每天都会出现在我的工作室门口，”他说，“我养不起它，但会喂它、陪它玩。我给它取名叫‘小黑’（Xiao Hei）。我们一起去散步。那是疫情期间，我正处在人生非常低谷的时期。看着它在田野里嬉戏，成了我的一种精神支柱。它的毛发全黑的，当它向远方奔跑时，便化作了一道黑色的闪电。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“然后有一天，它不再来了，”史国威继续说道，语气依旧坚毅而平稳，但面部线条却紧绷了起来，“起初我以为它还会出现，也许过几天就会回来，但它再也没有出现过。我在周围四处寻找，却始终没找到它。我花了很长一段时间才恢复过来。那是一段感觉一切都失去了控制、而我却无能为力的时期。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我眼眶湿润，移开视线，重新定格在那页纸上。有毒的白色夹竹桃毒云背后，那透亮的红色在审视下愈发浓烈。那是一种先于语言、先于思想甚至先于意识的红色。同样质感的红色，以各种色调和渐变贯穿于史国威的灌木、枝桠与顽石之中；在他的颜料覆盖下，它们坚硬的表面随之膨胀而又柔化——有时如骨骼般脆弱，有时又如皮肤与静脉般温润而娇嫩。这种矿物与动物质感之间的滑移，超越了形式上的相似，进入了一种与世界原初血肉相融的梅洛-庞蒂式纠缠。在中国东北与游牧民同行时，史国威曾看一个牧人解剖一头死鹿，其内脏被迅速且经外科手术般地排列并检查，以确定死因——是疾病、毒药，还是对人或羊群的其他威胁。牧人的镇定让史国威深为震撼：人、动物与土地之间的这种纽带如此深厚却又如此冷静——这是由生存所锻造的亲密关系，能够不事张扬地剖开一具躯体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_0945--1--2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_0944-4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "史国威北京工作室内的创作中作品一览。鸣谢艺术家及北京魔金石空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们再次起身，查看两件未完成的作品。其中一件里，一只火烈鸟脚踏船半掩在河畔的灌木丛后。这个节日道具既荒诞又威严——一个处于静止中的雄伟生灵，即便在休憩时，其优美的长颈也保持着庄重的神态。它那刺眼的粉红色渗入周围的植被，将船只、树叶和观者融为一个单一的感官连续体；人们仿佛能想象一个从野餐聚会中走散的孩子，拨开几片叶子，与这个迷人的生灵撞个满怀。不远处，另一件正在创作中的作品搁在画架上：透过一道树木织成的帘幕，可见水面上的带篷船里坐着一对伴侣。这种视角让我们置身岸上，窥视着一段我们无法介入且正在消退的亲密关系。这件半完成的作品，部分是彩色的，部分是灰度的，让人想起德勒兹式的水晶影像，其中“当下”与它正在变成的“虚拟过去”共存。史国威的相机记录了第一次相遇；他的色彩演绎了第二次相遇；而观者则更晚才抵达。通过感知、记忆与接受，影像不断累积着它的距离。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "节日承诺着时间的回归，但每一次回归都不是精确重合：人群在变，童年结束，心爱的动物消失了。史国威的色彩占据了那次回归与失落之间的缝隙：他画的不是本来的世界，而是曾经之物与无可挽回地消逝之物之间的间隙。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Michele Chan 是《ArtAsiaPacific》的执行主编。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
People

Shi Guowei: After the Festival

Shi Guowei sets down a box of cookies—a modest gift I had brought to Beijing from Hong Kong—and adds a platter of nuts and seeds, mugs for tea, bottles of Perrier. The spread is humble yet rich with quiet hospitality. I take a sip of water and prepare to record; beside me, an old harlequin cat, fur scruffy with age, climbs onto an empty chair and settles in for the conversation.

On the wall opposite hangs a large tableau, Drum (2026), from a new body of work soon to debut at Fotografiska Shenzhen this October. A constellation of red ceremonial drums sits on a nondescript floor, the base of an equally nondescript pillar visible in the composition’s upper register. The vantage is tilted downward, feeling accidental, except it isn’t—the instruments, scattered in derelict disorder, carry a disquieting, almost sentient charge.

“They were perhaps being played just moments ago,” says Shi, “then cast aside while people moved on to other festivities.” Shi’s method begins with a black-and-white photograph, which he paints over with water-based pigment in exacting, painstaking layers, in pursuit of what he calls an “authentic illusion.” Hand-coloring is a rigorous, largely obsolete technique, one that predates photography’s capacity for color. Trained as a photographer at Tsinghua University’s Academy of Arts & Design and later at the Fachhochschule Dortmund, Shi revives and redirects the age-old method—not toward verisimilitude, but toward displacing recorded fact for a particular emotional intensity, or what he terms “felt truth.” Here, the grooves in the grubby floor flare with scorched terracotta. The drums’ gilding has dulled with rust, their maroon lacquer worn and mottled by wear and stains. Yet their faces remain a stark, incongruous snow white, the characters 百年行 (“a hundred-year journey”) discernible atop.

Views of SHI GUOWEI ’s studio in Beijing. Courtesy the artist and Magician Space, Beijing.

“For some time I have found myself drawn to festivals,” Shi tells me, “but not their pageantry. What holds me is a quality I encounter around them, or after them.” His recent work marks a departure: after a decade spent rendering verdure, rock, and flora, he has turned his focus to the remnants of human celebration—its overflow, its sediment, its afterglow. In moments of isolation from crowds or in emptied corners of a carnival ground, Shi locates something resembling melancholy but stranger—subtler, yet somehow sharper. In Drum , it percolates most intensely in the barrels’ precisely calibrated plum-toned burgundy, faded through use yet all the more potent. That hue is echoed in a much smaller square study hung adjacent: a close-up of rock texture, the subject for which Shi is—for now, at least—best known. The stone, too, takes on a vital vermilion flush, its marbling rippling like sinew in raw flesh.

We walk over to another new work, Bridge (2026). Here the operant palette is green: a procession of round, scalloped cement forms appear to float on a pond, cast to resemble lotus leaves. The algae-filmed cement dons a jade cast while the water glimmers deep turquoise; upper left, brilliant chartreuse wavelets breach the serenity, lending the scene something at once magical and unsettling. The disturbance is produced by artificial light reflected from festivities nearby, just off-camera. “It was a tremendously crowded day,” Shi recounts. “I had to wait hours to capture this view without people.” The intrusion of yellow is deliberate: “On an ordinary day, the water would simply mirror a blue sky. But here there is something invasive. A quiet space has been forcibly entered. I wanted to convey that uneasy contrast.”

SHI GUOWEI , Drum , 2026, C-print and color ink, 126 x 135 cm (left); and Bridge , 2026, C-print and color ink, 145 x 126 cm (right). Courtesy the artist, Magician Space, Beijing, and Fotografiska Shenzhen.

Festivals divide time by returning. Each recurrence calls for celebration but measures all that passes in the interim—an illusion of progress and permanence undercut by an invisible accounting of absence and loss. A year, an anniversary, another gathering beneath lights—the shadows of which Shi inhabits. “Festivals are understood as collective occasions of happiness and hope,” he says. “But I am interested in what an individual experiences. Private feelings can diverge greatly from the noise and commotion. I want to ask what joy actually is.”

For years, Shi remained faithful to a vocabulary of motifs drawn from the natural world, accumulated largely during solitary walks in the mountains. I leaf through a catalog of earlier works: verdant shrubbery articulated in minute detail, severe faces of craggy cliffs, succulents alive and acerbic in saturated pastel tones. Their apparent stillness belies the peculiar temporality of their making. A photograph compresses an encounter into an instant; Shi reverses the process, re-inserting that isolated instant into the wayward currents of felt time. Over months, he revisits a single exposure through color and the repeated touch of his brush. There is something almost punitive in this sustained return, but also something relished: an obligation to look again, and feel again. The process amounts to a retrospective encounter, which chromatically loosens the image from the shutter’s grip; color stops being information and becomes qualitative, lived duration. Against an image culture organized around immediate edits and filters, Shi makes the almost foolish proposition that “some things require time.”

SHI GUOWEI , Fireworks II , 2025, C-print and color ink (left); and Garden II , 2024, C-print and color ink (right). Courtesy the artist, Magician Space, Beijing, and Fotografiska Shenzhen.

As I continue through the monograph, an instinctive recoil propels me past a page; catching myself, I double back. The image is an apparently innocuous close-up of a roadside thicket; beyond clusters of oleander in the foreground burns a scarlet horizon—muted yet feverish, almost malign. A brief silence passes, then the artist begins. “Some years ago, a puppy started appearing at my studio door every day,” he says. “I couldn’t afford to keep him, but I fed him and played with him. I named him Xiao Hei (‘Little Black’). We went for walks. It was during Covid, and I was at a very low place. Watching him frolic in the fields became a kind of lifeline for me. His coat was entirely black, and when he sprinted into the distance, he blurred into a flash of black lightning.”

“Then one day he stopped coming,” Shi continues, his tone still stoic and even, but his countenance tightening. “At first I thought he would show up again, perhaps after a few days, but he never did. I searched the surrounding areas but never found him. It took me a long time to recover. It was a period when everything felt beyond my control, and there was nothing I could do.”

Eyes welling, I avert my gaze, fixing it back on the page. The lucent red behind the poisonous clouds of white oleander intensifies under scrutiny. It is a red before language, before thought or even consciousness. The same quality of red, in various shades and gradations, courses through Shi’s bushes, branches, and stones; beneath his pigments, their obdurate surfaces swell and soften—brittle as bone at times, tender and fragile as skin and vein at others. This slippage between mineral and animal matter goes beyond formal semblance into a Merleau-Pontian entanglement with the primordial flesh of the world. While traveling with itinerant herding communities in northeastern China, Shi once watched a rancher dissect a dead deer, its organs swiftly and surgically arranged and examined to determine the cause of death—disease, poison, or some other threat to human or flock. Shi was struck by the herdsman’s composure: here was a bond between man, animal, and land so profound yet so unsentimental—an intimacy forged by survival, capable of opening a body without ceremony.

Views of works-in-progress at SHI GUOWEI ’s studio in Beijing. Courtesy the artist and Magician Space, Beijing.

We rise again to examine two unfinished works. In one, a flamingo boat emerges half concealed by riverside shrubbery. The festive prop is at once ludicrous and regal—a majestic creature at rest, its curved neck maintaining its stately composure even while in repose. Its acidic pink bleeds into surrounding vegetation, folding boat, foliage, and beholder into a single sensory continuum; one imagines a child wandering from a picnic party, parting some leaves to come face to face with an enchanting creature. Nearby, another work-in-progress rests on an easel: visible through a curtain of trees is a couple on a canopied boat on the water. The perspective keeps us onshore, peering into an intimacy we cannot enter, and one which is already receding. The half-completed piece, part colored and part grayscale, recalls the Deleuzian crystal-image, in which the present co-exists with the virtual past it is already becoming. Shi’s camera records the first encounter; his colors enact the second; and the viewer arrives later still. Through perception, memory, and reception, the image continually accrues its distance.

Festivals promise that time will return, but no return is exact: the crowd changes, childhood ends, a beloved animal disappears. Shi’s color occupies that lapse between recurrence and loss: he does not paint the world as it is, but the interval between what once was and what passes beyond recovery.

Michele Chan is managing editor at ArtAsiaPacific.

article_text:
フランク・ロイド・ライト代表作「タリアセン・ウエスト」で死亡事故。強風で飛ばされた屋根材が直撃

フランク・ロイド・ライト の旧居兼アトリエ、タリアセン・ウエストで10月16日、見学ツアーに参加していた男性が、強風で飛ばされた屋根材の直撃を受けて死亡した。アメリカ国立気象局によると、当時、周辺では時速約51キロに達する突風が観測されていた。

10月16日、アリゾナ州スコッツデールにある 建築 家 フランク・ロイド・ライト の旧居兼アトリエ、タリアセン・ウエストで、敷地内を歩いていた見学ツアー参加者の男性が、強風で飛ばされた屋根材の直撃を受けて死亡した。地元テレビ局 AZファミリー が伝えた。

亡くなったのは、ブラジルのパラナ教皇庁立カトリック大学（Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Paraná）学長、ロジェリオ・レナト・マテウッチ。スコッツデール消防局によると、事故が起きたのは現地時間午後2時ごろで、警察は事故の詳しい状況を調べている。

当日、地元テレビ局は「ファースト・アラート・ウェザー・デー」として、移動や安全に影響する悪天候への警戒を呼びかけていた。アメリカ国立気象局によると、事故当時、周辺では時速約35キロ（秒速約9.8メートル）の東風が吹き、時速約51キロ（秒速約14.3メートル）に達する突風が観測されていた。ほかのツアー参加者に被害は報告されていない。

タリアセン・ウエストは、ライトが1937年からアリゾナの砂漠に築いた冬季の自邸兼アトリエ。敷地面積は約199ヘクタールにおよび、弟子たちとの共同生活や建築教育の拠点でもあった。土地の素材と自然環境を生かした建築群は、世界遺産「フランク・ロイド・ライトの20世紀建築作品群」の構成資産に登録されている。

施設を管理するフランク・ロイド・ライト財団のCEO、ジョー・スペクターは、AZファミリーに寄せた声明で、次のように述べた。

「亡くなられた方のご家族と大切な方々に、心よりお悔やみ申し上げます。プライバシーを尊重し、関係当局の調査を妨げないため、これ以上の詳細は公表しません」

財団はInstagramでも、スコッツデール警察が事故を把握していると説明し、施設の一般公開を当面休止すると発表した。（翻訳：編集部）

article_text:
Amazon Prime Video has found much success in the YA space with series such as The Summer I Turned Pretty , We Were Liars , Elle and Sterling Point .

Now, the streamer is turning its attention to a similar, but slightly older, and raunchier audience for its next batch of programming: the New Adult.

Related Stories

‘Fourth Wing’ Finds Its Violet & Xaden: Esther McGregor & Emilio Sakraya To Lead Prime Video Series

Netflix Assembles YA Stars Past, Present & Future For End Of Summer Bash Event To Reassert Presence In The Genre

It has already had hits in this space, which features characters aged 18-29, rather than younger teenagers between ages 12 to 18, with shows such as its adaptations of Elle Kennedy’s Off Campus and Carley Fortune’s Every Summer After , and has lined up a show based on Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill book series and a TV adaptation of Lucy Score’s Things We Never Got Over that dovetail into the growing tier.

New Adult, which is thought to have emerged as a term in the late 2000s thanks to publisher St. Martin’s Press, targets readers and viewers aged 18 to 29 and bridges the gap between Young Adult (YA) fiction and Adult fiction.

Watch on Deadline

New Adult also offers explicit sex scenes (hello, Off Campus ). The online book community calls this spice, and it ranks how high each book’s spice level is depending on the amount of explicit sexual scenes. For instance, a story with less detail is sometimes called a “closed-door” romance because, like in movies or TV, the act is merely alluded to, but not fully shown.

RELATED: Prime Video Teases Summer Slate Of YA Originals, Book Adaptations & More From ‘The Love Hypothesis’ To ‘Clashing Through The Snow’

Off Campus , often labeled a YA series, fits into New Adult. The first season follows the romance between Briar University’s hockey captain, Garrett Graham (Belmont Cameli) and quiet songwriter and college junior, Hannah Wells (Ella Bright). It launched in May and became Prime Video’s third most-viewed debut season ever behind The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and Fallout , and was renewed for a second season ahead of its launch.

Similarly, Every Year After was renewed for a second season after its June bow. The TV series, which comes from Amy B. Harris and Leila Gerstein, is based on Carley Fortune’s eponymous book, the sequel of which will serve as the basis of Season 2. While the first book starts with Sam Florek (Matt Cornett) and Persephone “Percy” Fraser (Sadie Soverall) meeting in their adolescence, the time jump in the show’s first season includes the characters in their late twenties. The second book, One Golden Summer , tells the love story of Sam’s brother Charlie Florek (Michael Bradway), who is 35, and his love interest, Alice Everly, who has yet to be cast for Season 2 of the show, is 33 in the book.

“We’re always coming of age, and I love that. I see it in my mom’s generation, I see it with people in their 80s still entering new phases of what life looks like,” Fortune told Deadline in an interview tied to Every Year After ‘s release . “I think the 30s are particularly interesting because you have made so many decisions that have set you up for where you are, and it is a great time to sit back or be forced to take a look at what those decisions, where they have put you, and is that where you [want to] be? The stakes go higher.”

Next up are Rose Hill and Things We Got Over . Rose Hill is a four-book series of contemporary romance novels that feature interconnected stories set in the same fictional town: Wild Love , Wild Eyes , Wild Side , and Wild Card .

RELATED: Everything We Know About Prime Video’s ‘Rose Hill’ Series Adaptation So Far

The first season of the series will follow the story from the first novel, Wild Love , which centers on best friends and neighbors West Belmont (Jake Weary), a rancher with commitment issues, and brooding record label owner Ford Grant (Sean O’Pry), who’s long carried a torch for West’s sister, Rosie (Hannah Galway). And when country-pop star Skylar Stone (Sadie Dickerson) breezes into their rugged mountain town, the heat gets turned way up in this romantic family drama.

HOW ABOUT THIS – The streamer is already casting the Rose Hill series in anticipation of success. Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway, Jake Weary, and Sadie Dickerson have already been cast as the couples that lead the first two books , Wild Love and Wild Eyes . A few key characters from the latter half of the quartet have also been cast. Prime Video has a history with this strategy, having also banked on buzz around Off Campus by intertwining the love stories of the main four hockey teammates from the very beginning of the series. While Season 1 focuses on Hannah and Garrett, Stephen Kalyn’s Dean DiLaurentis and Mika Abdalla’s Allie Hayes were heavily teed up to take over for Season 2, and easter eggs were planted for the other two teammates’ love stories in Season 1.

The same pattern applies to Things We Got Over , based on the first novel in Lucy Score’s trilogy of romances. While the first installment features a love triangle between Naomi Witt (Molly Griggs) and the Morgan brothers, Nash (Tommy Martinez) and Knox (Matthew Noszka), the following two books delineate to center two more Knockemout romances. Knockemout is the small town in Virginia where the series is set. Soft spoiler alert, the second book features the romance of the brother Naomi doesn’t end up with, and the third features local librarian Sloane (Sarah Jeffery) and Lucian (Sean Teale).

RELATED: Everything We Know About Prime Video’s ‘Things We Never Got Over’ Adaptation So Far

While Rose Hill is marketed as a series of single dad romances, and the Knockemout trilogy follows two brothers and their best friend, these two series are considered women-led — a genre that is still undersupplied across film and television, according to a report from Luminate .

Rose Hill and Things We Never Got Over also both deal with more mature themes including parenthood. In Wild Love , the first Rose Hill book, O’Pry’s character Ford Grant realizes he has a biological child after sperm donation on a whim to get concert tickets. Things We Never Got Over forces parenthood on Naomi, whose twin sister Tina leaves her daughter Waylay (Megan Stott) behind for her more responsible sister to take care of. While Off Campus is set in college, the book series still deals with heavier topics as well, like Hannah’s rape and Garrett’s father’s abuse in Season 1.

It’s not a coincidence that Off Campus , the Rose Hill books and Things We Got Over trilogy all come from the same romance publisher: Bloom Books. The imprint even uses obsession in its marketing for books it brings to life.

RELATED: The Summer 50-Something Female Friendships Took Over Streaming With ‘Five Star Weekend’ & ‘Ride Or Die’s Surprise Success

Rose Hill leans western like Netflix’s recently cancelled Ransom Canyon , and Prime Video is aiming to rope in more than if not the same audience that fell in love with Off Campus . These shows should also appeal to older millennials given that a number of the characters in these books skew older. That being said, the New Adult category strikes the balance between those not yet old enough to pay for their own Prime Video or Amazon Prime accounts (new subscribers) and audiences of older women who may already have said subscriptions, which may have factored into the cancellation of female friendship centered buddy comedy Ride Or Die .

Should the streamer continue with Obsessed Fest, it will be interesting to see how it markets its expanding slate of book adaptation romances. It will also be interesting to see if social media fan edits, which Head of Marketing for Amazon and MGM Studios Sue Kroll admitted to staying up late watching at the inaugural Obsessed Fest, will diverge when more of the New Adult shows arrive on Prime Video.

Amazon is also leaning into New Adult on the film side: Ana Huang’s Gods of the Game trilogy has been optioned for a trio of film adaptations by Amazon MGM Studios , Lauren Asher’s Throttled will get a feature adaptation from the studio as well. Both Huang’s and Asher’s books are published by Bloom.

RELATED: Which Ali Hazelwood Books Are Becoming Movies? ‘The Love Hypothesis,’ ‘Deep End’ & More

They follow successful film adaptations of non-Bloom books like Casey McQuiston’s college-set Red, White & Royal Blue — which is getting a sequel film —starring Taylor Zakar-Perez as 21 year-old Alex Claremont-Diaz and Nicholas Galitzine as the slightly older Prince Henry plus Ali Hazelwood’s The Love Hypothesis starring Lili Reinhart and Tom Benton, which is set in graduate school at Stanford University, and Hazelwood’s Love, Theoretically.

Then , there’s Fourth Wing, a romantasy series based on Rebecca Yarros’ Empyrean series, which centers 20-year-old Violet Sorrengail (to be portrayed by Esther McGregor ) . A huge book in the romantasy genre, Fourth Wing does fall into the New Adult age range category, but romantasy — a combination of romance and fantasy — often includes much more elaborate world-building. Amazon MGM Studios will also stretch its film romance offerings with the dark romance adaptation of Butcher & Blackbird , which has just set its lead cast .

Amazon is not alone in spotting the growing New Adult trend. Netflix, which has been in on the YA trend for many years , has lined up an adaptation of Fortune’s This Summer Will Be Different , and Shawn Levy is developing a series based on Elsie Silver’s Chestnut Springs novels . The streamer has also optioned the rights to Ana Huang’s Twisted Love and its sequels for a TV series adaptation.

RELATED: Co-Founders Of Magic Hour Entertainment And Rebelle Media Plus Author Duo Christina Lauren Advise Studios & Streamers To Devote Resources To “Elevated” And “Prestige” Romance Through Casting, Chemistry & More

On the film side, Netflix also has Guarding Stars , based on Katherine Center’s The Bodyguard and In a Holidaze , based on the book by Christina Lauren, coming out in November and December , respectively. The two holiday stories feature characters in the older New Adult age bracket. Shawn Levy’s 21 Laps and Alex Cooper’s Unwell Productions are also behind a feature film adaptation of Ali Hazelwood’s Deep End .

Apple TV’s got The Buccaneers going for it, but that book adaptation falls more in the vein of period romances like Bridgerton . Apple TV also recently won the rights to Rebecca Yarros’ upcoming novel Peculiar Stars , which publishes November 17. Hulu took a big swing with an attempt to adapt Sarah J. Maas’ A Court of Thorns and Roses , but the rights have reverted back to Maas, who has two more books in that romantasy series on the way.

Ahead of Amazon’s Obsessed Fest over the summer, Peter Friedlander, Head of Global TV, Amazon MGM Studios said there was a halo effect from Off Campus on Every Year After . “One success begets another,” he said just a day before Every Year After received its second season renewal, like Off Campus had done. Sterling Point ’s Season 2 renewal signals continued domination in the YA space for the streamer too, as do the upcoming second seasons of We Were Liars and Elle and The Summer I Turned Pretty ‘s concluding film.

title_original: Finding Vermeer in Unexpected Places
editorial_title_zh: 在意想不到的地方寻找维米尔
editorial_excerpt_zh: 历史学家露丝·伯纳德·耶泽尔（Ruth Bernard Yeazell）在《维米尔的来世》（“Vermeer’s Afterlives”）中写道，艺术家、电影人、诗人乃至艺术市场本身，至今仍带有这位荷兰画家的影响痕迹。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "图书评论", "links": [{"text": "Book Review", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/tag/book-review/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "在意想不到的地方寻找维米尔", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "历史学家露丝·伯纳德·耶泽尔（Ruth Bernard Yeazell）在《维米尔的来世》（“Vermeer’s Afterlives”）中写道，艺术家、电影人、诗人乃至艺术市场本身，至今仍带有这位荷兰画家的影响痕迹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/size/w1200/2026/10/vermeer-and-van-meegeren.jpg", "alt": "在意想不到的地方寻找维米尔", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "听起来可能有些奇怪，约翰内斯·维米尔（Johannes Vermeer）的名气是一个相对较近的现象。这位以精致、神秘的室内场景而闻名的荷兰画家在1675年去世时债台高筑，年仅43岁，此后不久便湮没无闻。直到19世纪中期，巴黎评论家泰奥菲尔·托雷（Théophile Thoré）重新发现他的作品之前，维米尔在艺术史的编年史中几乎只是一个微不足道的注脚。“这是我们在法国不了解的人，而且非常值得为人所知！”这位作家在1866年这样宣告。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "托雷被维米尔吸引的原因，与他至今仍令博物馆参观者着迷的原因如出一辙：他那数量有限的署名画作——迄今约有35幅——以及至今依然模糊的生平，引发的问题多于答案。但在他去世后的三个半世纪里，维米尔神秘的作品也激发了丰富的视觉艺术、电影、诗歌和文学。", "links": [{"text": "still-hazy biography", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/the-fruitless-search-for-vermeers-personal-god/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/2026/10/gobillard.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些艺术回响正是学者露丝·伯纳德·耶泽尔（Ruth Bernard Yeazell）的《维米尔的来世》（Vermeer’s Afterlives，2026）一书的焦点。该书通过对在其神话化阴影下创作的作品进行仔细考察，图文并茂地探讨了这位艺术家持久且极为广泛的影响。从丹麦画家威廉·哈默修伊（Vilhelm Hammershøi）静谧的画布，到20世纪的实验电影和感性的当代诗行，耶泽尔一丝不苟地分类并分析了这位代尔夫特画家的图像学——尤其是他那反复出现、由附近窗户透入的日光柔和照亮的孤独女性形象——以及他对开放式解读而非单一叙事的执着追求。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Book Review", "links": [{"text": "Book Review", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/tag/book-review/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Finding Vermeer in Unexpected Places"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Artists, filmmakers, poets, and the art market itself still bear traces of the Dutch painter’s influence, writes historian Ruth Bernard Yeazell in “Vermeer’s Afterlives.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/size/w1200/2026/10/vermeer-and-van-meegeren.jpg", "alt": "Finding Vermeer in Unexpected Places", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As strange as it may sound, Johannes Vermeer’s fame is a relatively recent phenomenon. The Dutch painter known for his exquisite, enigmatic interior scenes fell into obscurity shortly after he died deeply in debt at only 43 years old in 1675. article_text:
Book Review

Finding Vermeer in Unexpected Places

Artists, filmmakers, poets, and the art market itself still bear traces of the Dutch painter’s influence, writes historian Ruth Bernard Yeazell in “Vermeer’s Afterlives.”

As strange as it may sound, Johannes Vermeer’s fame is a relatively recent phenomenon. The Dutch painter known for his exquisite, enigmatic interior scenes fell into obscurity shortly after he died deeply in debt at only 43 years old in 1675. Vermeer was barely a footnote in the annals of art history until the mid-19th century, when the Parisian critic Théophile Thoré rediscovered his work. “Here’s someone we don’t know in France, and who very much deserves to be known!” the writer proclaimed in 1866.

Thoré was drawn to Vermeer for the same reason he still fascinates museumgoers today: His small selection of attributed paintings — some 35 to date — and still-hazy biography spark more questions than answers. But in the three and a half centuries since his death, Vermeer’s mysterious works have also inspired a wealth of visual art, cinema, poetry, and literature.

These artistic echoes are the focus of scholar Ruth Bernard Yeazell’s Vermeer’s Afterlives (2026), a richly illustrated exploration of the artist’s enduring and remarkably widespread impact through a careful survey of works made in his mythologized shadow. From Danish painter Vilhelm Hammershøi’s hushed canvases to experimental 20th-century film and sensual contemporary verse, Yeazell meticulously catalogs and analyzes the Delft painter’s iconography — especially his recurring solitary female figures gently illuminated by daylight filtered through nearby windows — and persistent commitment to open-ended interpretation over a singular narrative.

article_text:
Meg Onli and Zack Winokur will curate the 83rd Whitney Biennial, set to open in March 2028.

Onli joined the Whitney in 2023 as curator-at-large before being named Nancy and Fred Poses curator. She co-curated the 2024 Whitney Biennial alongside Chrissie Iles. Prior to joining the Whitney, she served as co-director and curator of the Underground Museum in Los Angeles and as the Andrea B. Laporte associate curator at the Institute of Contemporary Art at the University of Pennsylvania. In 2010, Onli founded the Black Visual Archive, a project dedicated to reviewing contemporary Black visual culture.

Zack Winokur is the artistic director and co-founder of AMOC* (American Modern Opera Company), a collective of singers, dancers, instrumentalists, writers and producers. In 2025, AMOC* organised a five-week performance festival across Lincoln Center, New York. From 2024 to 2026, Winokur was the first producing artistic director of Little Island, New York, and previously served as artistic director of NYPopsUp, a statewide initiative that aimed to reopen the performing arts following the COVID-19 pandemic.

article_text:
CLAMP presents “Studio Nudes,” an extensive group exhibition exploring artists’ use of live models in their work from the 1940s to the present. Bringing together an array of photography, drawing, and painting, the show investigates how modern and contemporary practitioners challenge, amend, and reframe classical artistic traditions.

The history of the studio nude in art spans from ancient academic practices to the current day. In Ancient Greece, the male nude was celebrated through athletics and sculpture, representing civic glory, heroism, and divine perfection.

Conversely, during the Middle Ages, nudity was largely restricted and tied to theological concepts of shame, sin, vulnerability, or Last Judgment scenes. The Renaissance revived classical proportions, bringing male and female models back into the studio—though public display of the artworks required mythological, historical, or religious disguises to remain socially acceptable. By the 17th and 18th centuries, drawing live models became the core of formal artistic training. In the mid-19th century, Édouard Manet shattered standards of propriety with “Olympia” (1863), replacing the safe, distant mythical goddess with a real Parisian sex worker staring defiantly at the viewer, sparking massive public outrage. This opened the path for raw, unidealized nudes stripped of all pretexts, allowing modern artists to use the life-model studio setup for their formal experiments with composition, color, and form.

“Studio Nudes” features artworks from the mid-20th century to the present that engage with these historic antecedents. Mapping a clear lineage from formal mid-century Modernism to subversively charged contemporary works, the exhibition organizes the artists into distinct thematic and stylistic dialogues:

Historical Allusions Shot in his home studio, Daniel Handal’s “Cranach Nudes” reference classical antiquity’s Greek and Roman myths, along with religious subjects from the Renaissance. Similarly, Curtice Taylor’s cyanotype prints pay homage to late 19th-century Victorian depictions of the male figure. Robert Calafiore employs custom, hand-built pinhole cameras to create large-scale, one-of-a-kind chromogenic prints. Also inspired by classical Greco-Roman art, Calafiore photographs male nudes; his analogue techniques serve as a deliberate step back from the endless flood and speed of digital technologies.

Modernist Foundations and Identity By the 1940s, George Platt Lynes’s photographs of male and female nudes were not only celebrations of the ideal form, but also bold, Modernist experiments in lighting and composition. Expanding on the studio portrait tradition to examine identity, Lissa Rivera’s images of her nonbinary romantic partner depict bodies historically underrepresented in art. And like Platt Lynes, her works such as “Experiment with Gels” function as exercises in color and composition as she deeply mines the history of 20th-century film, photography, and painting.

Academic Studies vs. Final Expressions Studio studies from the nude figure by master draftsmen Paul Cadmus and later Mark Beard stand as rigorous academic exercises originally created in preparation for tempera or oil paintings on panel and canvas. In contrast, Jack Balas and Francisco De la Barra’s works on paper bypass the preparatory stage, serving as the definitive, final forms of artistic expression in their own right.

The Self-Reflexive Lens Breaking down the traditional boundary between artist and subject, Peter Berlin in the 1970s and Roberto Bocci in the late 1980s and early 1990s turned the lens entirely on themselves, staging their own bodies as the central models of interest.

Contemporary Provocations Modern and contemporary practitioners such as James Bidgood, Bruce of Los Angeles, Jim French, John Button, Victor Carnuccio, Christopher Makos, Amos Badertscher, and Paul Solberg reframe the conventions of the studio nude. Infusing raw energy and sexuality into expressive artworks from the past fifty years, these cross-generational dialogues frequently incorporate themes of identity, bodily autonomy, and the legacy of the artist-model relationship.

Featured artists: Amos Badertscher, Bruce of Los Angeles, Christopher Makos, Curtice Taylor, Daniel Handal, Francisco De la Barra, George Platt Lynes, Jack Balas, James Bidgood, Jim French, John Button, Lissa Rivera, Mark Beard, Paul Cadmus, Paul Solberg, Peter Berlin, Robert Calafiore, Roberto Bocci, and Victor Carnuccio

article_text:
Law Roach is ready for an even bigger close-up.

The celebrity stylist, whose clients include Zendaya, Kim Kardashian and Celine Dion, says he’s “absolutely” ready to try some acting.

“When a director sees something for me,” Roach told me Thursday night at the InStyle Imagemaker Awards. “I want to try everything. If I’m terrible at it, at least I tried.”

Related Stories

MK2 Films Acquires Dardenne Brothers, Archipel 35 Film Library to Expand Its Heritage Footprint (EXCLUSIVE)

He’s certainly worked with enough A-list actors to get some guidance, no? “I’ve also worked with some of the greatest singers of all time, but that doesn’t mean I’m going to try to sing,” Roach cracked.

Popular on Variety

The celebrity stylist tells me he "absolutely" wants to try to do some acting: "If I’m terrible at it, at least I tried." https://t.co/uI3oZE64AG via @variety #justforvariety #redcarpet pic.twitter.com/JCq7rf1VdM — Marc Malkin (@marcmalkin) October 17, 2026

Roach has made cameos as himself in “The Devil Wears Prada 2” and the Kate Hudson Netflix sitcom “Running Point.” He has also served as reality television judge on “Legendary,” “America’s Next Top Model,” “Project Runway” and “RuPaul’s Drag Race.”

Also on the carpet, fellow Imagemaker honoree (and sometimes Roach client) Priyanka Chopra Jonas talked about reuniting with her “Baywatch” co-star Zac Efron for “Judgment Day,” the upcoming Nicholas Stoller Amazon MGM Studios comedy that also stars Will Ferrell, Regina Hall and Fortune Feimster.

“I had a blast. I went in there to learn and had a great time,” Jonas said. “I’m just sitting there and watching everyone.”

I also talked to Priyanka Chopra Jonas about working with Zac Efron, Will Ferrell, Regina Hall and more in the upcoming Nicholas Stoller comedy “Judgement Day.” How much did Priyanka break? Here’s what she had to say… https://t.co/sFLD2lL7bq @variety #redcarpet #PriyankaChopra pic.twitter.com/miLJOkA4QD — Marc Malkin (@marcmalkin) October 17, 2026

Efron stars as a newly released prison inmate who takes a TV courtroom judge and his television cast and crew hostage. The cast also includes Michael Peña, Billy Eichner, Jimmy Tatro, Heidi Gardner, Bobby Cannavale and Bill Camp.

Was Jonas breaking all the time? “No, no, I’m a professional,” she quipped. “Maybe twice. Once with Will, for sure and once with Regina. She said something and I was just done. Fortune said something too and I was really trying hard … I’m a girl that comes from drama, so to be surrounded by all of these amazing comedians and actors who are so easy with comedy, it was so cool to witness.”

editorial_title_zh: 吉安卡洛·库库眼中的色彩：都灵马林潘萨画廊举办展览
editorial_excerpt_zh: 都灵马林潘萨画廊举办的吉安卡洛·库库（Giancarlo Cuccù）个展，回顾了一项以色彩为基础的探索，交织着马尔凯大区的风景记忆与绘画材质的层叠。文章提到：吉安卡洛·库库眼中的色彩：都灵马林潘萨画廊…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "2026年10月17日至10月30日，都灵马林潘萨画廊（Galleria Malinpensa）将举办吉安卡洛·库库（Giancarlo Cuccù）的个人展览《色彩的脉动流转》（L’influire pulsante del colore），由莫尼亚·马林潘萨（Monia Malinpensa）策展。该项目汇集了一系列精选作品，贯穿了艺术家创作中反复出现的核心主题，从风景到肖像、从静物到人物，将色彩作为构图结构元素的核心地位凸显出来。", "links": [{"text": "Galleria Malinpensa", "url": "https://latelaccia.it/"}, {"text": "Torino", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/torino/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "库库出生于都灵，父母来自马尔凯大区。他的童年前几年在马尔凯大区度过，位于蒙泰维东科巴特市镇的科利纳努奥娃（Collina Nuova）村庄。1967年他永久返回该大区并搬到费尔莫。他与马尔凯大区风景的关系依然是他绘画中始终如一的参照点之一，不仅作为创作主题，也是记忆与个人经历之所在。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "从风景到人物", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他与绘画的结缘可追溯至20世纪50年代末，当时库库在木板上创作了他的第一幅风景画。在接下来的几年里，他的作品涉足了不同的主题：小巷、肖像、人物、人体、风景以及水墨画。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在20世纪60年代末至70年代期间，通过对不同艺术流派和语言的研究，他的探索得到了拓展。1976年，在他首次前往巴黎的旅行期间，他直接接触到了法国后印象派绘画以及那些对现代先锋派发展产生深远影响的艺术实践。与此同时，他深入研究了希皮奥内（Scipione）、吉诺·罗西（Gino Rossi）和瓦尔林（Varlin）等艺术家的作品，并不断与马尔凯风景展开对话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在21世纪头十年，他还曾在塞雷（Céret）居住，这是一个与欧洲先锋派历史紧密相连的地方，并在那里继续他对色彩与物质的探索。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/img4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "《有房屋的风景》，布面油画（应为纸板油画），46,6×65 厘米，2026年", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "作为构建元素的色彩", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在展览呈现的作品中，色彩占据了核心功能。它不仅仅用于定义表面和主体，还组织了绘画空间，并有助于构建画作内部的张力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "莫尼亚·马林潘萨将库库的绘画形容为“充满强烈的表现力”，其中色彩变成了“一种真正深沉而具结构性的价值”。因此，通过通过层层叠加构建出的厚重色彩材质，日常现实、风景与人体被转化呈现出来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Dal 17 al 30 ottobre 2026, alla Galleria Malinpensa di Torino , è in programma L’influire pulsante del colore , mostra personale di Giancarlo Cuccù , a cura di Monia Malinpensa . Il progetto riunisce una selezione di opere che attraversano alcuni dei nuclei ricorrenti della ricerca dell’artista, dal paesaggio al ritratto, dalla natura morta alla figura, mettendo al centro il ruolo del colore come elemento strutturale della composizione.

Nato a Torino da genitori marchigiani, Cuccù trascorre i primi anni di vita nelle Marche, nella frazione di Collina Nuova, nel comune di Monte Vidon Combatte, prima di tornare stabilmente nella regione nel 1967, quando si trasferisce a Fermo. Il rapporto con il paesaggio marchigiano resta uno dei riferimenti costanti della sua pittura, non solo come soggetto ma anche come luogo della memoria e dell’esperienza personale.

Dal paesaggio alla figura

L’incontro con la pittura risale alla fine degli anni Cinquanta, quando Cuccù realizza un primo paesaggio su legno. Negli anni successivi il suo lavoro attraversa soggetti differenti: vicoli, ritratti, figure, nudi, paesaggi e disegni a china.

Tra la fine degli anni Sessanta e gli anni Settanta, la sua ricerca si amplia attraverso lo studio di autori e linguaggi diversi. Nel 1976, durante uno dei suoi primi viaggi a Parigi, entra in contatto diretto con la pittura francese del post-impressionismo e con le esperienze che avrebbero segnato lo sviluppo delle avanguardie moderne. Parallelamente approfondisce il lavoro di artisti come Scipione , Gino Rossi e Varlin , continuando a confrontarsi con il paesaggio marchigiano.

Negli anni Duemila soggiorna anche a Céret, luogo legato alla storia dell’avanguardia europea, dove prosegue la propria ricerca sul colore e sulla materia.

Il colore come elemento costruttivo

Nelle opere presentate in mostra, il colore assume una funzione centrale. Non interviene soltanto per definire superfici e soggetti ma organizza lo spazio pittorico e contribuisce alla costruzione della tensione interna dell’immagine.

Monia Malinpensa descrive la pittura di Cuccù come «Ricca di intensa energia espressiva», nella quale il colore diventa «Un vero e proprio valore intimo e strutturale». Il rapporto con il quotidiano, con il paesaggio e con la figura umana viene così tradotto attraverso una materia cromatica densa, costruita per stratificazioni.

La tecnica dell’olio su tela e dell’olio su cartone pressato consente all’artista di lavorare sulla consistenza della superficie e sulla forza del gesto. La pennellata resta visibile e partecipa alla costruzione delle forme, mentre il colore viene utilizzato per accentuare profondità, ritmo e presenza fisica dei soggetti.

La memoria della terra marchigiana

Accanto alla componente più strettamente pittorica, il lavoro di Cuccù mantiene un rapporto costante con l’esperienza biografica e con i luoghi in cui si è formato. Il paesaggio marchigiano ritorna come riferimento visivo e culturale, assumendo un ruolo che supera la semplice rappresentazione geografica. Nella lettura proposta dalla curatrice, la terra marchigiana diventa infatti «luogo dell’identità», capace di mettere in relazione osservazione del presente, memoria e vissuto personale.

Ritratti, figure e nature morte partecipano dello stesso processo: soggetti differenti vengono ricondotti a una ricerca che utilizza la pittura per registrare esperienze, stati emotivi e frammenti della quotidianità. L’influire pulsante del colore propone così una ricognizione sul lavoro di Giancarlo Cuccù attraverso una pittura fondata sul rapporto tra costruzione formale, memoria e materia cromatica, ripercorrendo una ricerca sviluppata nell’arco di diversi decenni.

article_text:
Oscar-nominated star Eric Roberts is leading the first vertical drama to be revealed from Alon Shtruzman and Scott Einbinder ‘s nascent Hollywood outfit New Short Media .

Created by Gev Miron and Charlie Parker, It’s My Party and I’ll Die If I Want To will be released as both an episodic vertical series and feature film intended for theatrical release.

The project follows Anna, who races to conceal the shocking truth about her best friend’s death on the night of her 21st birthday. As guests arrive and long-buried secrets begin to surface, Anna confronts betrayal and family revelations that threaten to turn a celebration into a night of lies and fatal consequences. Roberts, who was Oscar nominated for 1985’s Runaway Train, stars alongside Merrick Hanna ( America’s Got Talent ), Neela Jolene ( Acting Coach Nightmare ), Ryker Baloun ( Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy ) and actor and digital creator Nicholai Perrett.

Related Stories

Kristen Brancaccio To Direct Microdrama & Feature Adaptations Of Claren Hammond's Short Story 'Summer Session'

Moby, Hannah Stocking & Adam Rose Set For Microdrama Slate From TikTok & Made By Us Studios

Roberts is already featuring in a separate vertical project, Billionaires’ Broken Vow , which premiered at America’s first microdrama festival earlier this month.

Watch on Deadline

Former Keshet International boss Shtruzman and ex-Cristal Pictures Co-CEO Einbinder launched New Short Media earlier this year , one of a new wave of vertical drama platforms tapping into the in-vogue medium.

Shtruzman said: “Vertical drama isn’t replacing Hollywood. It’s adding a new engine at a time when traditional television and streaming are contracting. Micro-vertical is a new language of storytelling, and this fast-growing category is bringing new investment and new jobs into the entertainment industry.”

article_text:
Il 17 ottobre 2026 ha inaugurato la Shanghai Grand Opera House , il nuovo teatro d’opera progettato dallo studio norvegese Snøhetta lungo il fiume Huangpu, a Shanghai . Selezionato attraverso un concorso internazionale nel 2016 e sviluppato a partire dal 2019 insieme a un gruppo di partner specializzati, il progetto si estende su una superficie di 146.786 metri quadrati e riunisce tre auditorium per complessivi 4.200 spettatori. Una grande copertura bianca, che si piega in una scala elicoidale accessibile al pubblico e raggiunge una terrazza panoramica affacciata sul fiume e sullo skyline della città.

Un complesso culturale che comprende spazi per le prove e la produzione, ambienti espositivi, attività formative, ristoranti e servizi di accoglienza.

Il pubblico può quindi attraversare l’edificio e raggiungerne la copertura anche senza assistere a uno spettacolo, utilizzando il teatro come spazio di passaggio e di permanenza.

«Concepito come un paesaggio culturale aperto, coniuga una sede per le arti performative di livello mondiale con uno spazio pubblico accessibile, invitando residenti e visitatori a interagire con la cultura, l’architettura e la vita urbana. Radicato nello spirito di apertura, scambio e innovazione di Shanghai, il progetto amplia l’accesso alla cultura, creando al contempo una nuova piattaforma per l’espressione artistica e la partecipazione civica», ha affermato lo studio architettonico.

Il progetto è stato sviluppato da Snøhetta insieme all’East China Architectural Design & Research Institute (ECADI), con il contributo di competenze locali e internazionali in ambito architettonico, teatrale e acustico. Tra gli aspetti considerati figurano anche l’integrazione del paesaggio come parte fondamentale del progetto e l’impiego della luce naturale come protagonista dell’architettura.

Una copertura che diventa spazio pubblico

La copertura che si sviluppa in un movimento continuo attorno al volume architettonico, fino a trasformarsi in una scalinata monumentale, collega il piano terra alla terrazza superiore e accompagna la salita con vedute progressivamente più ampie sul fiume Huangpu e sul paesaggio urbano, attribuendo al tetto una funzione ulteriore rispetto alla protezione degli ambienti interni e rendendolo un luogo destinato alla sosta e all’incontro.

«Non è semplicemente la superficie superiore dell’edificio, ma diventa suolo pubblico, punto di osservazione, luogo d’incontro e palcoscenico per la vita della città. L’appartenenza pubblica si costruisce attraverso l’esperienza, quando le persone possono entrare, muoversi e usare un luogo secondo le proprie modalità».

La forma dell’edificio risponde al corso del fiume e al ritmo della città, mentre i diversi livelli pubblici sono collegati attraverso percorsi che mantengono una continuità visiva tra architettura e paesaggio. Le superfici vetrate favoriscono l’ingresso della luce naturale e rendono leggibile la relazione tra gli ambienti interni e il contesto circostante; all’esterno, il rivestimento prevalentemente bianco contrasta con le tonalità più scure degli spazi destinati alle rappresentazioni.

L’idea di un’architettura culturale attraversabile anche al di fuori della programmazione richiama un progetto precedente dello studio, la Norwegian National Opera and Ballet di Oslo , inaugurata nel 2008 e anch’essa con una copertura accessibile. A Shanghai, questo principio viene ripreso su una scala diversa e con una rotazione spirale che subito richiama il movimento: il ventaglio cinese, il corpo nella danza, il corso dello Huangpu. «Non siamo mai stati interessati a realizzare un edificio che rappresentasse un singolo oggetto o potesse essere ridotto a un’unica immagine simbolica», hanno affermato gli architetti.

Le tre sale

All’interno del complesso, le tre sale sono progettate per accogliere produzioni differenti per dimensioni e impostazione scenica. La Harmony Hall è l’auditorium principale da 2.000 posti e si sviluppa su cinque livelli – tra platea e balconate – con l’obiettivo di contenere la distanza tra spettatori e palcoscenico. I palchi laterali contribuiscono a creare una relazione più ravvicinata con la scena, mentre la configurazione degli spazi e la scelta dei materiali rispondono alle esigenze acustiche della rappresentazione operistica; l’esterno chiaro lascia qui spazio a tonalità rosso scuro e a superfici dalla consistenza più marcata.

L’ambiente è concepito come un volume unitario, nel quale geometrie e materiali concorrono alla diffusione della voce umana e alla qualità dell’ascolto.

Le altre due sale ampliano le possibilità d’uso della struttura: il Soar Theatre, con 1.200 posti, è destinato a produzioni di dimensioni più contenute, dall’opera barocca e classica all’operetta e al teatro; l’Open Stage, da 1.000 posti, dispone invece di configurazioni adattabili del palco e delle sedute, per accogliere anche formati sperimentali e non convenzionali.

«Perché l’architettura non è completa quando si vince un concorso, e nemmeno quando la realizzazione è terminata. Continua a trasformarsi attraverso la collaborazione, la costruzione, l’uso e, infine, l’appartenenza pubblica».

title_original: Jogen Chowdhury, ‘Towering Pillar’ of Indian Modern Art, Has Died at 87
editorial_title_zh: 乔根·乔杜里，“印度现代艺术的巨柱”，享年87
editorial_excerpt_zh: 乔根·乔杜里是孟加拉艺术运动最后的幸存者之一。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔根·乔杜里是一位印度领先的现代画家，其具象作品强调人性，于10月25日在加尔各答一家医院去世，享年87岁。印度媒体报道称，乔杜里在过去一年多时间里一直遭受一种罕见的血液癌症的折磨。", "links": [{"text": "Jogen Chowdhury", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/jogen-chowdhury/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在他去世后，社交媒体上纷纷送来哀悼。在X平台上，西孟加拉邦首席部长苏文杜·阿迪卡里称赞乔杜里为“我们文化世界的一根擎天柱”，其艺术遗产将“永垂不朽”。同样，居住在加尔各答的著名画家萨米尔·艾奇将他的去世视为“个人的损失”，并代表孟加拉艺术运动的一个章节的结束。这一20世纪初的艺术运动起源于英属印度时期的加尔各答（前称加尔各答）和萨钦尼克坦，随后在整个印度次大陆蓬勃发展，受到印度独立运动的推动。", "links": [{"text": "praised", "url": "https://x.com/SuvenduWB/status/2114245809835528425?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2114245809835528425%7Ctwgr%5Eaa2273c52215b0fd90329e770b145f0f6f4d27b4%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.newindianexpress.com%2Fstates%2Fwest-bengal%2F2026%2FOct%2F25%2Feminent-painter-jogen-chowdhury-dies-at-87-3"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为对当时印度艺术教育中西方现实主义主导地位的回应，孟加拉艺术运动借鉴了印度传统艺术形式，如莫卧儿细密画、田园主题以及历史与神话的交织。萨钦尼克坦的红土地貌，乔杜里在那里有一处住所，是这一运动的特别灵感来源。由于印度、日本和欧洲之间蓬勃的文化交流，立体主义和日本现代艺术的审美贯穿了这一运动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔杜里以其线条作品而闻名，这些作品在印度艺术中独具特色的触感和表现力方面表现出色。他经常使用交叉阴影技法，巧妙地扭曲人体，将他们推向漫画风格，但这并非出于嘲讽，而是为了可视化心理内部。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这些人物由装饰性的随意性和表现性扭曲共同塑造，并充满了一种奔放的性感，”印度艺术评论家R·希瓦·库马尔曾写道。“乔杜里的艺术充满暗示；它不应被我们已有的知识、经验和记忆所框定，但也不能被叙述化，否则会使其感官独特性被削弱。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔根·乔杜里出生于1939年2月16日，当时属于未分割的孟加拉地区的法里德普尔的达哈帕拉村。（英国占领势力在1947年第二次按宗教划分将孟加拉分割，此前在1905年曾有过一次失败的尝试。）他描述了自己的创作性、贵族式的成长环境：他的母亲以擅长阿尔帕纳绘画而闻名，他的父亲是一位画家和雕塑家。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他于1955年进入加尔各答政府艺术与工艺学院学习。他从1955年至1960年也在该学院接受培训，之后于1960年代在巴黎的法国国家美术学院学习，1968年返回印度。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Jogen Chowdhury , one India’s leading modern painters whose figurative oeuvre foregrounded humanity, died at a hospital in Kolkata on October 25. He was 87. Indian media reports that Chowdhury had been suffering from a rare blood cancer for more than a year.

Condolences have poured in on social media in the wake of his death. Writing on X, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari praised Chowdhury as a “a towering pillar of our cultural world,” whose artistic legacy would be “immortal through the ages.” Likewise Samir Aich, a prominent painter based in Kolkata, mourned his death as “personal loss” and representative of a chapter closing on the Bengal School of Art, an early 20th-century art movement that originated in Kolkatta (formerly Calcutta) and Shantiniketan during the British Raj, and then flourished across the Indian subcontinent, buoyed by the Indian Independence Movement.

Reacting in part against the dominance of Western realism in Indian art eduction at the time, the Bengal School of Art drew on Indian traditional art forms, such as Mughal miniatures, pastoral themes, and the intermingling of history and mythology. The distinctive red earth landscape of Santiniketan, where Chowdhury had a home, was a particular inspiration. Elements of Cubism and Japanese modern art sensibilities were threaded throughout the movement, owing to a thriving cultural exchange between India, Japan, and Europe.

Chowdhury was renowned for his line work, which excelled in the tactile, expressionistic quality unique to Indian art. He often used a cross-hatching technique to delicately distort the human figure, pushing them to caricature not as a mockery, but as a means of visualizing psychic interiors.

“The figures are wrought by a combination of decorative wilfulness and expressive distortion and are imbued with an effusive sensuality,” Indian art critic R. Siva Kumar once wrote. “Chowdhury’s art is rich in suggestions; it is to be apprehended without bracketing our fund of knowledge, experience or memories, but also cannot be narrativised without trivialising it, without depleting its sensory particularities.”

Jogen Chowdhury was born on February 16, 1939, in Daharpara village in Faridpur, then a region in undivided Bengal. (British occupying forces partitioned Bengal along religious lines for the second time in 1947, after a failed attempt in 1905.) He described a creative, aristocratic upbringing: His mother was renowned for her skill in Alpana drawings, and his father was a painter and sculptor.

He enrolled in to the Government College of Art & Craft, Kolkata in 1955. He also trained at the Government College of Art & Craft from 1955 to 1960 and later at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris in the 1960s, returning to India in 1968.

In 1972, Chowdhury served as a curator at the Art Gallery of Rashtrapati Bhavan, the official residence of India’s president. In April 2014, he entered politics, winning election to the Rajya Sabha, India’s upper house of Parliament, as a member of West Bengal’s Trinamool Congress. He served until April 2020.

Chowdhury’s art accolades include the Prix de la Jeune Peinture in Paris in 1966 and recognition at the Second Havana Biennial in Cuba in 1986. In 2001, he received the Kalidas Samman from the government of Madhya Pradesh in recognition of his artistic contributions. In 2012, he was awarded the Banga Bibhushan, the highest civilian honor conferred by the government of West Bengal.
excerpt_original: Jogen Chowdhury was one of the last surviving members of the seismic Bengal School of Art.
